newsitem.title: UK: Ofgas decision on discount pricing met with "shock".
newsitem.headline: Ofgas decision on discount pricing met with "shock".

text.p: Calortex, a partnership between Calor Gas and Texaco Inc, said on Wednesday that it had greeted with "shock and disappointment" the decision by UK gas industry regulator Ofgas to allow discount pricing by British Gas Trading.
BGT launched its ValuePlus scheme in early March in the first pilot area to be opened to domestic gas competition, covering the south western counties of Devon, Cornwall and Somerset.
It offers a discount of 12 percent off the standard gas tariff to customers who pay by direct debit, an increase on the normal 6 percent discount automatically offered to direct debit customers.
Under the 1995 Gas Act, the monopoly holder can only cut prices to meet "established competition," so Ofgas' decision means it accepts that effective competition is now in place in the pilot area.
But Calortex said in a statemet it is the leading independent domestic mains gas supplier in the area, and has only 8 percent of customers there.

This compares with BGT's 80 percent market share, the company said, adding that it sees ValuePlus as "a deliberate attempt by the former monopoly supplier to strangle competition and long-term customer choice."

"We strongly believe that ValuePlus is a predatory pricing technique, which is also highly discriminatory and represents the very worst of 'cherry picking,'" said Neil Lambert, joint General Manger of Calortex.

"This decision from Ofgas appears to demonstrate a U-turn on its previous policy of encouraging competition in the mains gas market and to fly in the face of the Regulator's obligations under the Gas Act to secure effective competition."
Lambert added that competition cannot be said to have been established until at least 50 percent of the market is supplied by competitors to BGT.

"We are totally bemused as to the logic of this decision. With in excess of 12 independent companies sharing only 20 percent of the total market in the South West, in no way can competition be said to be established."
